procedure: content/text/glossary/terms/ carries 15 stems with both a .md and a .org file. For each: whitespace-insensitive full-text diff against the .md twin. Where identical (modulo trailing blank lines) or where the .org body is empty (property drawer + title + date only, no prose), the .org contributed nothing the .md did not already carry -- removed. Where the .org carried real, distinct content, left both files untouched and recorded why.

kept_both_deliberately.reason: agency.org is an org-roam node from a different, older personal knowledge-graph vein (#+index: psychology!agency; relations table linking to psychology/condition/agentic/sovereignty) -- a different sense of 'agency' than the relationality-specific reading in agency.md (the capacity to enact relating). Not the same concept restated; a name collision. Not this sweep's call to merge or relocate.

relating.org (2025-08-25, one sentence: 'Relating is acting that makes relationship between one thing and a different thing') reads, on a literal parse, as the substance-first view relating.md explicitly refuses ('not a connection between pre-existing things but the directed act that constitutes its terms'). Possibly an early, superseded formulation rather than a duplicate -- philosophically loaded enough that silent deletion risks the information-loss law. Left for owner review.

relation.org ('A relation is a thing that does any relating to another thing') reads relation as an active relater; relation.md reads relation as the stabilized structural residue relating leaves behind. Same tension as relating.org -- not clearly the same claim reworded. Left for owner review.

relational-dynamics.org is live Emacs org-roam operational machinery (an elisp org-roam-db-query block plus #+include of introducing-relational-dynamics.org), not static prose -- a different kind of artifact than relational-dynamics.md, not a duplicate of it in any format this sweep can compare.

verification: grep across the whole repository (excluding lib/legacy/) for markdown-link or literal-path references to each removed filename found none pointing at these files from live content; the only hits were an unrelated personal-services-section org-roam vault's self-references to its own same-named files.
